貿.meaning: In a desert town, a <part>shellfish</part> pushes through the <part>saloon doors</part> with a sack of pearls and walks out wearing a cowboy hat. Next a cowboy walks in with a lasso and leaves with a pearl. The bartender just keeps the doors swinging: this saloon runs on <kanji>trade</kanji>.
貿.on: One day a prospector rolls in a whole <sound>bou</sound>lder and swaps it for a single pearl.

涯.meaning: An old <part>quarry</part> fills with rain until <part>water drops</part> brim at every ledge, and it becomes a lake so wide that from one cliff you can't see the other. A boy on the edge squints at the thin far line where grey water meets grey sky: his first <kanji>horizon</kanji>.
涯.on: His <sound>gui</sound>de dog sits beside him, nose pointed at that faraway line.
涯.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs, as the <sound>te</sound>nnis ball the dog dropped bobs off towards it.

嘱.meaning: A lighthouse keeper going on holiday whispers every rule into the <part>mouth</part> of her parrot: wind the lamp, feed the cat, wave at ships. The bird was hatched in the lamp room and will never <part>belong</part> anywhere else. There's no one she'd rather <kanji>entrust</kanji> with the light.
嘱.on: The stand-in keeper gets a <sound>shock</sound> when the parrot squawks 'Wind the lamp!' at midnight.
嘱.kun: Then it squawks the cat's orders too, and the cat leaps up in <sound>shock</sound> and knocks over the oil can.

璧.meaning: At a <part>chili stall</part> in the night market, the seller grinds her hottest red pepper until the powder glows, then rolls it round a tiny <part>jewel</part> again and again. By midnight it's a smooth, perfectly round red ball that never stops spinning on the counter: a fiery <kanji>sphere</kanji>.
璧.on: She sells it in a little <sound>hex</sound>agon box lined with silk.
璧.kun: A <sound>ta</sound>co seller swaps two tacos for it, a gift for his <sound>ma</sound>ma.

肯.meaning: Two astronauts argue on the <part>moon</part> about which way is home, back and forth for hours, until one plants a <part>stop</part> sign in the dust between them. They stare at it, burst out laughing, shake gloved hands and at last reach <kanji>agreement</kanji>.
肯.on: They seal the deal by sharing one ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, frozen solid.
肯.kun: Their <sound>ga</sound>rlic-scented <sound>en</sound>gine coughs, and the moon <sound>jee</sound>p rolls home.

芯.meaning: A camper's candle has lost its string, so she twists a blade of <part>grass</part> and pokes it right through the <part>heart</part> of the wax. It burns with a green flame and smells like a summer lawn. Her best camping trick yet: a grass <kanji>wick</kanji>.
芯.on: She leans in to sniff it, and hot wax drips onto her <sound>shin</sound>.

践.meaning: A palace <part>spear rack</part> stands by the gate. At midnight a sleepwalking giant comes by, and one huge <part>foot</part> comes down on it with a crunch, flattening every spear. He snores on, never noticing where he chose to <kanji>tread</kanji>.
践.on: The <sound>sen</sound>try on guard just salutes the giant's passing toe.
践.kun: Then he wraps the bent spears in his <sound>fu</sound>ton and goes back to bed.

癒.meaning: A tiny <part>spaceship</part> crash-lands in a farmer's <part>leaky shed</part>, its alien pilot sobbing with a broken <part>heart</part>. The farmer brings tea, the rain drips a lullaby on the roof, and by morning the alien is humming and the ship's dents have popped out. The old shed is good at <kanji>healing</kanji>.
癒.on: The farmer squeezes a <sound>yu</sound>zu into the alien's tea.
癒.kun: Her pet <sound>ee</sound>l wraps round the ship's hull like a bandage.

猿.meaning: A <part>ball gown</part> sweeps across the palace dance floor with nobody's head poking out of the top. From the balcony, a guard lowers a <part>fishhook</part> on a line, snags the hem and lifts. Out tumbles a giggling, long-tailed gatecrasher: a <kanji>monkey</kanji>.
猿.on: It escapes by leaping onto a fire <sound>en</sound>gine parked outside.
猿.kun: As it goes, it drops a silk <sound>sa</sound>ri and a <sound>ru</sound>by ring it pinched from the ball.

措.meaning: A sailor hauls up her <part>anchor</part> and finds a chest from <part>antiquity</part> hooked on it, crusted with barnacles. She's dying to open it, but a storm is rolling in. With a sigh she shoves it under her bunk to <kanji>set aside</kanji> for later.
措.on: When the storm passes, she opens it sitting on her squashy <sound>so</sound>fa.
措.kun: Inside, an <sound>o</sound>ctopus is curled round a heap of old coins.

霜.meaning: A night of light <part>rain</part> falls on two neighbours' cars parked nose to nose. By dawn both windscreens are white and feathery, and the neighbours scrape away in <part>mutual</part> misery, each blaming the other's car for the cold. It's only <kanji>frost</kanji>.
霜.on: One tries rubbing it off with a warm, sudsy bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
霜.kun: <sound>She</sound> gives up, grabs a <sound>mo</sound>p and scrubs till the glass squeaks.

棺.meaning: A vampire <part>bureaucrat</part> sleeps all day in a long box carved from one old oak <part>tree</part>, with a 'Do Not Disturb' form stamped on the lid in triplicate. At sunset he climbs out, straightens his tie and goes to file papers. His bed is a <kanji>coffin</kanji>.
棺.on: He pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to his cape before work.

肘.meaning: An astronaut tries a <part>golf club</part> swing on the <part>moon</part>, but her stiff suit won't bend halfway along her arm. Whoosh: she misses the ball, spins and floats over. Back at base she fits a hinge to the suit's weak spot: the <kanji>elbow</kanji>.
肘.on: She blows a bubble of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum as she tightens the screws.
肘.kun: In the <sound>hea</sound>t of the sun the hinge works fine, and she drives off in her moon <sound>jee</sound>p.

虎.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> painted on a circus banner gets bored, grows a pair of <part>legs</part> and steps right off the canvas, still flat as paper. It prowls the ring and roars like a rustling page, and the crowd claps anyway for the paper <kanji>tiger</kanji>.
虎.on: Then it curls up to nap beside a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala in the next tent.
虎.kun: The koala offers it a <sound>to</sound>ffee and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

藩.meaning: On a small island, every family takes its <part>turn</part> to guard the well: they cover it with cut <part>grass</part> against the sun and count the <part>water drops</part> so nobody takes more than their share. Hundreds of cousins, one well, one rule: they are a <kanji>clan</kanji>.
藩.on: Whoever guards the well gets a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey as thanks.

伎.meaning: A hiker hangs her jacket on a <part>coat hook</part> by a stream, snaps a <part>branch</part> off a willow and whittles it into a tiny boat for a crying boy who lost his toy in the water. No badge for it, no photo, just a good <kanji>deed</kanji>.
伎.on: The boy gives her a big brass <sound>key</sound> to his treehouse in return.
伎.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>, hu<sound>zzah</sound>!' he cheers, as the little boat sails off: a real skill.

諦.meaning: The <part>emperor</part> bans every <part>speech</part> that isn't flattering. One day his parrot, who never learned to flatter, squawks, 'Your crown is crooked!' The court gasps; the emperor checks a mirror and laughs. At last someone told him the <kanji>truth</kanji>.
諦.on: He fixes the crown straight with a strip of sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
諦.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sighs, giving up on flattery, and shares a <sound>ki</sound>wi and some <sound>ra</sound>men with the parrot.

謙.meaning: A famous opera singer is giving two shows <part>concurrently</part>: one for the grand hall, one for a single janitor sweeping backstage. She stops her big <part>speech</part>, walks down and sits on his bucket to sing just for him. A star happy to come down to anyone's level: she will <kanji>condescend</kanji>.
謙.on: Her little dog howls along from his <sound>ken</sound>nel in the wings.
謙.kun: Afterwards she bows low to the <sound>herri</sound>ng seller, the <sound>coo</sound>k and the <sound>du</sound>ck that lives by the stage door.

畔.meaning: A farmer cuts her <part>rice field</part> in <part>half</part> with a raised strip of mud, so the ducks on the left can't squabble with the ducks on the right. Every morning she walks along its narrow top like a tightrope, arms out. The ducks call it the wall; she calls it the <kanji>paddy ridge</kanji>.
畔.on: Halfway along she stops to dip a finger in a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey.
畔.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasps, as a <sound>ze</sound>ppelin drifts low over the ridge and the ducks all duck.

礁.meaning: An undersea volcano spits out a <part>stone</part> so hot its edges <part>char</part> black, and it cools into a jagged lump just under the waves. Ships steer round it, coral grows over it, and by spring a family of little fish has opened a café on it: the new <kanji>reef</kanji>.
礁.on: Every evening the clownfish put on a <sound>show</sound> there for passing turtles.

窟.meaning: A mouse digs a little <part>hole</part> in a hillside and keeps going. The rock should stop her, but it starts to <part>yield</part>, crumbling soft as cake, until her tunnel opens into a vast hall where her squeak echoes back a hundred times: a <kanji>cavern</kanji>.
窟.on: In the dark pool at its centre floats one lonely black <sound>coot</sound>.
窟.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k, <sound>wah</sound>, <sound>ya</sound>hoo!' squeaks the mouse, and the echo shouts it all back.

菊.meaning: A gardener wants the biggest flower at the fair. She ties a <part>wrap</part> of <part>grass</part> round one fat bud and feeds it a bowl of <part>rice</part> every day. On the morning of the fair it bursts into hundreds of thin golden petals: a prize-winning <kanji>chrysanthemum</kanji>.
菊.on: The judge, a <sound>ki</sound>wi farmer, has his <sound>coo</sound>k pin the gold ribbon on it.

紳.meaning: A <part>monkey sign</part> hangs over the tailor's shop. Inside, a monkey threads a needle and sews a suit of gold <part>thread</part> for a visiting king, then bows deeply as he tries it on: 'It fits you perfectly, <kanji>sire</kanji>.'
紳.on: The king kneels to try the trousers and bumps his <sound>shin</sound> on the counter.

坑.meaning: A baker digs in the <part>soil</part> behind her shop for her grandmother's buried <part>cake stand</part>. She digs, and digs, and digs, until she looks up and sees only her dog's face peering down from the edge. She's not in the garden any more; she's at the bottom of a <kanji>pit</kanji>.
坑.on: The dog lowers her an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne on a string.

仙.meaning: High on a <part>mountain</part>, an old man owns nothing but a <part>coat hook</part> hammered into a rock. At night he hangs his only coat on it, and by day he hangs the passing clouds there to dry. He hasn't come down in fifty years: the happy <kanji>hermit</kanji>.
仙.on: Once a year a <sound>sen</sound>try climbs up to check on him and goes home with a cloud.

須.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> with painted <part>whiskers</part> sits on the edge of the bath and lectures like a grandpa: 'You ought to scrub behind your ears. You ought to rinse twice.' Every squeak is a rule. That bossy duck always knows what you <kanji>ought</kanji> to do.
須.on: 'And after your bath you ought to eat your <sound>su</sound>shi,' it squeaks.
須.kun: Next rule: you ought to do a <sound>Su</sound>doku in <sound>be</sound>d after <sound>kara</sound>te class.

慕.meaning: A snowman stares at the <part>sunset</part> every evening, melting one <part>trickle</part> at a time, because he's in love with the sun and can never get close to it. Each night he's a little smaller and still gazing west. That's <kanji>pining</kanji>.
慕.on: His only friend, a little <sound>bo</sound>nsai on the windowsill, tries to cheer him up.
慕.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p wanders by and offers him a cold <sound>ta</sound>co.

枕.meaning: A <part>sleeper</part> camping in the woods forgets her pillow, so she rests her head on a mossy root of a <part>tree</part>. The tree feels sorry for her and grows the moss thicker all night, soft as feathers. By dawn it's the comfiest <kanji>pillow</kanji> in the forest.
枕.on: She wakes up with moss stuck to her <sound>chin</sound>.
枕.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma <sound>coo</sound>ks <sound>ra</sound>men for breakfast beside the tree.

搾.meaning: A sailor wants juice but has no press, so she jams an orange into a <part>hole</part> in the ship's <part>coat rack</part> and leans the iron <part>anchor</part> on top. Juice sprays everywhere, even into the parrot's eye. One mighty <kanji>squeeze</kanji>.
搾.on: She waters her potted <sound>suc</sound>culent with the drips.
搾.kun: <sound>She</sound> pours what's left into a <sound>bo</sound>ttle for the parrot.

諮.meaning: Before every <part>speech</part>, the mayor turns to the <part>next</part> seat, where her goldfish sits in its bowl. It opens its <part>mouth</part>: bloop. She nods and tears up page two. She never says a word in public without stopping to <kanji>consult with</kanji> the fish.
諮.on: When it disagrees, the goldfish hides behind a tiny knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
諮.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>! Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' it bloops, and the mayor breathes again.
